title: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct - Civic Education - Interpersonal Relationships
exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following statements provides the most accurate definition of an **interpersonal relationship**?
options: The legal contract between a corporate business and its newly hired employees.
The social association, connection, or affiliation established between two or more people.
The official diplomatic ties maintained between sovereign nations.
The interaction between an individual citizen and the country's armed forces.
questions.explain: An **interpersonal relationship** is a social connection, association, or affiliation between two or more people based on mutual interaction, shared interests, blood relations, or love.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: The relationship that naturally exists among individuals who share the same bloodline, ancestry, or marital ties is classified as a...
options: platonic relationship.
peer relationship.
familial relationship.
professional relationship.
questions.explain: **Familial relationships** are formed through biological blood ties, adoption, or marriage (e.g., relationship between parents and children, or between siblings). Other types include peer, platonic, and professional relationships.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios describes a **platonic relationship**?
options: A strict and formal interaction between an employer and an employee
An intimate and highly romantic relationship between two lovers
A deep, non-sexual friendship between two individuals
A biological connection between parents and their offspring
questions.explain: A **platonic relationship** refers to a close, affectionate, and trusting friendship between two people (often of the opposite sex) that is purely spiritual and non-sexual in nature.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following is a crucial skill required to promote and sustain healthy interpersonal relationships?
options: Rigid adherence to personal opinions without compromise
Active listening and effective communication
Promoting malicious gossip among close associates
Intimidation and emotional manipulation of peers
questions.explain: Skills that promote interpersonal relationships include **active listening, effective communication, empathy, tolerance, and mutual respect**. These foster understanding and trust between individuals.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: **Inter-communal relationship** can best be defined as the social, cultural, and economic interaction that exists between...
options: individuals belonging to the same nuclear family.
two or more distinct towns, villages, or ethnic groups.
different countries trading in the international global market.
members belonging strictly to the same political party.
questions.explain: While interpersonal relationships deal with individuals, **inter-communal relationships** refer to the interactions, associations, and cooperations that occur between two or more distinct communities, towns, or ethnic groups.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: A positive inter-communal relationship is highly essential for a nation because it primarily promotes...
options: the domination of smaller communities by larger ethnic groups.
the cultural extinction of minority languages and traditions.
secessionist movements by marginalized regional groups.
peace, mutual security, and socio-economic development.
questions.explain: Good inter-communal relationships encourage peaceful coexistence, reduce the chances of conflict, promote inter-marriage, and foster an environment where **socio-economic development and national security** can thrive.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Two neighbouring communities previously at odds decided to jointly finance and build a central market. This cooperative action is most likely to result in...
options: mutual economic growth and an improved standard of living.
increased local poverty and uncontrolled inflation.
fierce political rivalry and renewed boundary tensions.
the total abandonment of their distinct cultural heritage.
questions.explain: Building shared infrastructure (like a central market) is a practical example of positive inter-communal relations. It creates trade opportunities, boosts commercial activities, and directly leads to **mutual economic growth** for both communities.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: **Inter-communal conflict** typically arises when neighbouring communities...
options: engage frequently in inter-tribal marriages.
clash violently over disputed land or scarce natural resources.
share their respective cultural festivals peacefully.
form a joint neighborhood vigilante security network.
questions.explain: Inter-communal conflicts are violent clashes or disputes between different communities. These conflicts are predominantly caused by disputes over **land boundaries, grazing rights, scarce resources, or chieftaincy titles**.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: When a severe inter-communal conflict breaks out, what is the most appropriate and sustainable method of resolving the dispute?
options: Deploying armed vigilante youths to forcefully reclaim the disputed area
Cutting off all communication and trade links indefinitely
Engaging in constructive dialogue, negotiation, and mediation
Seeking immediate military intervention from foreign countries
questions.explain: The most effective and lasting way to resolve inter-communal conflicts is through non-violent dispute resolution mechanisms such as **dialogue, negotiation, mediation, and arbitration**, rather than resorting to violence or military force.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 1: National Values, Rights, Citizenship & Social Conduct
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: An independent, neutral third party who is invited to actively assist two warring communities in reaching a mutually acceptable peaceful settlement is acting as a...
options: mediator.
litigant.
dictator.
mercenary.
questions.explain: In conflict resolution, a **mediator** is a neutral third party whose role is to facilitate dialogue between conflicting parties and help them negotiate a peaceful, mutually beneficial agreement.
